title: Harmony v2: octave-aware chord analysis that rewards good chords and inversions, steering feedback, and a chord-following EQ
description:
User (2026-09-27): discord is the main reason mash-ups fail. Favour combinations that make good and interesting chords (inversions, 7ths/9ths), give feedback on how to transform a clip (which way to steer), and shape the spectrum so notes outside the target chord are filtered out, 'kind of like autotune but not exactly'. The user wants full control of key, tuning and chord expression (the language already has slash chords IV/3, Bb/D, voicing and role bass).

Today's checker (check.py) folds each stem's HPCP into 12 pitch classes per beat and only penalises clashes (a pair interval kernel, plus chord clash). It can't see octaves, so no inversions, and it never rewards a good chord.

Pieces:
1. Octave-aware analyzer: per-beat note salience by constant-Q plus harmonic templates (basic-pitch can help). It recognises the sounding chord, including inversion and extensions, and adds a positive chord-quality term (matches the target chord and bass; interesting extensions; voice-leading smoothness) next to the clash penalty.
2. Steering report per clip x scene: clash for all 12 transpositions (a rotation of the pitch profile), a wrong-note list with frequencies per chord, a cents correction, and the bars that fit; structured output for the optimizer, agents and the web UI.
3. Chord-following EQ, an engine effect that re-targets on every chord change. It must be PARAMETERIZED for creative use (user): notch tolerance/width (cents or Q), depth (dB), mode (cut non-chord tones / boost chord tones / both), harmonics protected (so a chord tone's own partials aren't cut), frequency range, glide at chord changes, mix; all automatable. Tight = invisible cleanup; wide or resonant = a tuned, chordal effect. Plus an optimizer 'notch' op fed by the wrong-note list.
4. Target control: key, tuning reference, chords with inversions/voicings from the score.

Validate against the user's ear: the Emerge swap they loved scored only 3rd of 4 on the current checker.

# Harmony v2: octave-aware chord analysis, steering feedback, and a chord-following EQ

Design for Kanbus epic `apricitus-445cae`. Read-only research against `origin/develop`
(`7bc24fc`, the main checkout is on `develop` and current); nothing was edited or committed.
Every claim about the code below was checked against the source unless marked **unverified**.
The experiment (section 5) rendered eight 8-bar windows with `--stems` into the scratchpad
(352 MB peak), analysed them with a prototype, and deleted them.

## 0. Decisions at a glance

| Question | Decision | Why (short) |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | CQT, 36 bins/octave (3 per semitone), C1–B7, hop 512 at 22.05 kHz, then **NNLS harmonic-template decomposition** into per-semitone note activations. Not additive templates, not basic-pitch as the primary. | Additive templates hallucinate a root a fifth below a sounding fifth (the prototype heard C/E as Am7, section 5.3); NNLS explains E4 with E2/E3 already present and puts nothing on A. basic-pitch stays a cross-check: it is an ML black box we can't parameterise, and its note events already exist in every manifest for the *clip*, not the rendered stem. |
| Ground truth first | Pitched single-note tracks (`stems.json` `pitch`, e.g. `Ab1 (pinned)`) are **not** re-analysed: their sounding notes come from the compiled timeline. Only loops (`transpose auto|follow|N`) get audio analysis. | The bass is what inversions hinge on, and the engine already knows exactly what it played. Every prototype run that re-detected the bass from audio mis-heard it (C, then A#). |
| Time grid | The score's beat grid (as today), plus a per-span aggregate; the first 100 ms after every chord change is skipped for chord recognition (not for clash). | Chord recognition needs stable notes; the `smear` metric already covers the change itself. |
| Tuning | Per stem: parabolic sub-bin fit on each frame's fundamental peak, median over frames (validated: +29.8 ¢ for a synthetic +30 ¢ note). Per note: the same fit per extracted note. | `librosa.estimate_tuning` and Essentia's `TuningFrequencyExtractor` both read the whole spectrum; on a bass stem they are noise. |
| Chord recognition | Root × quality (the 12 qualities in `apricity-theory` plus 6, m6, 9, maj9, m9, add9 as extensions) × bass; scored on the combined note activations, with the score's bass when known. | Extensions are what the user wants rewarded; `Quality` in `crates/apricity-theory/src/chord.rs` stops at sevenths, so 9ths must be recognised as "a 7th chord plus a 9th" until the chord model grows. |
| Objective | `objective_v2 = consonance_v1 − guards + 10 · Q̄`, `Q̄` the mean per-span chord-quality in 0..1. `Q` only earned on beats with tonal mass above a floor and with the bass sounding. | Weight 10 is the smallest that puts the Emerge swap first *and* keeps the cycle-2 incumbent first (section 5.2); 20 breaks cycle 2. Q on the same activations the energy/density guards see means muting can't buy it. |
| Chord-following EQ | One Rust effect, `harmonic`, a bank of peaking biquads re-targeted per 32-frame block from a chord timeline the **compiler** embeds in the spec; three modes (`cut`, `boost`, `both`); `tolerance` in cents; `harmonics N` protects chord-tone partials. Not STFT masking. | Biquads slot into `process_chain`'s existing 32-frame automation path, are bit-exact and cheap, and have no phase smearing or musical-noise artifacts; a `both` mode with a wide tolerance and high boost is the "tuned resonance"/comb the user asked to play with. |
| Production language | **Rust** for everything that runs: the analyzer and steering report in a new crate `apricity-harmony` (CLI `apricity check` / `apricity steer`, wasm, UniFFI, PyO3 or JSON), the effect in `apricity-dsp`/`apricity-engine`. **Python** only for the reference implementations, the parity tests, the validation numbers, and the offline ML (basic-pitch, beat tracking, CLAP) whose outputs the Rust analyzer reads from manifests and sidecars. | User direction (2026-09-27): the runtime goes into the Swift app, the web and Python; nothing in the loop may call Python. |
| DSP in Rust | `rustfft` (pure Rust, builds for wasm and iOS) + a hand-written sparse-kernel CQT (~200 lines) + hand-written Lawson–Hanson NNLS (~120 lines) + the parabolic peak fit (~20 lines). No ndarray/nalgebra. | Nothing in `Cargo.lock` does any of this today; `apricity-dsp` has zero dependencies and should stay that way, so the FFT dependency lives in `apricity-harmony`. Section 2.7 has the cost. |
| Phase 1 | The Rust analyzer core (`apricity-harmony`: CQT, NNLS, notes, cents, chord recognition, `Q`, `objective_v2`, `steer.json`) with the Python reference and parity tests, `apricity check`/`steer` in the CLI, `bass`+`events` in `stems.json`. No effect yet. | It's the piece the optimizer and the user's ear can validate now; the effect needs its parameters tuned by ear once the report tells us where the wrong notes are. |

## 1. What exists, verified, and what the experiment showed

**Checker (`analysis/apricity_analyze/check.py`).** Per stem, per beat: Essentia HPCP (12 bins,
harmonics=8, 40–5000 Hz) weighted by RMS × (1 − spectral flatness ≥ 40 Hz). `beat_clash` =
Σ pairs `c_i·K·c_j` / (total mass)² + an undiluted bass-vs-root semitone term; `INTERVAL_K`
gives m2 and M7 1.0, tritone 0.7, M2 0.35, m7 0.3 (lines 31–37), doubled when either stem is the
bass. `chord_clash_terms` (line 230) only penalises non-chord tones. `consonance = 100·(1 − mean
clash)`; guards subtract points (energy, mute, density, coverage 2/violation, tuning 2/stem >8 ¢).
There is **no positive term** and no octave: `Stem.chroma` is `(n_beats, 12)`.

Two things the experiment surfaced about the pair kernel (section 5.1 details):

- Under `VImaj7 (Fmaj7)` the top finding for every candidate is *"bright's E a semitone below
  the bass F"*. E is the written major seventh. The pair kernel scores a M7/m2 between stems at
  1.0 ×2 regardless of what the chord says, so a correctly voiced maj7 is the checker's worst case.
  v2 must read the pair kernel *through the chord*: a chord-tone/chord-tone pair costs 0 unless it
  is a real register problem (section 2.5).
- `bass_root_penalty` and `choose_bass` do the right thing here (`low` has `pitch = "Ab1 (pinned)"`).

**stems.json** (`crates/apricity-cli/src/render.rs:171–207`): `sample_rate`, `tempo`, `meter`,
`key`, `offset_beats`, `length`, `harmony[] {start_beat, end_beat, label, chord, chord_tones}`,
`tracks[] {name, pitched, kit, out, sends, pitch}`. The span's **bass is not written**; the chord
name from `Chord::name()` (`chord.rs:186`) does include `/bass` when it differs from the root, so
a Python reader can parse it, but Phase 1 should add an explicit `"bass"` field (one line in
`stems_manifest`). `chord_tones[0]` is the root (`Chord::pitch_classes`, `chord.rs:125`).

**Solver (`crates/apricity-theory/src/harmony.rs`).** `solve()`'s `total(choice)` is
Σ per-voice solo score + `coverage` (lines ~118–122); the solo score is chord-tone / scale-tone /
outside weights on the *voice's own* pitch-class profile, plus role and continuity. **Confirmed:
no term looks at two voices together**, so `transpose auto` cannot avoid a clash with another
part; the `runners_up` it reports are the per-chord alternatives the steering map should re-score
with the other parts present. `apricity explain` prints them (`bright −5 st tonic→E ... next best:
−2 (−0.16), +0 (−0.23)` under `VII (G)` for the Emerge swap).

**Chord model.** `Quality` (`chord.rs:10`): Major, Minor, Diminished, Augmented, Sus2, Sus4,
Dominant7, Major7, Minor7, MinorMajor7, HalfDiminished7, Diminished7. `Chord { root, quality,
bass: Option<PitchClass> }`; `voiced()` puts a slash bass lowest. **No 9ths, 6ths or add chords**
in the model or the DSL: "interesting extensions" can be *heard* and *rewarded* in v2, but not
*written* as a target until the chord model grows (open question 1).

**Effects and automation.** `Effect` enum (`crates/apricity-score/src/score.rs:142`): Eq, Comp,
Limit, Reverb, Delay, Drive, Lofi, NoiseGate, Width, Filter. `process_chain`
(`crates/apricity-engine/src/master.rs:475`) cycles the loop buffer so tails wrap, then per effect:
if it has automation lanes, it re-derives the effect's spec every **32 frames** via
`automated_effect()` (line 407) and calls `MasterChain::set`; otherwise the original one-shot
path runs unchanged ("No automation: use original path unchanged", with a bit-identical test
`no_automation_output_equals_previous_behavior` in `mix.rs`). It receives `frames_per_beat` and
`offset_beats` but **not the harmony**. `Biquad` (`crates/apricity-dsp/src/fx.rs:12`) has
`Peak { hz, db, q }` and a `response_db()`; `Eq` caps at `MAX_BANDS` (8 in the docs). The DSL's
effect keyword tables are `TRACK_LINES`/`GROUP_LINES`/`MASTER_LINES`/`EFFECTS`
(`crates/apricity-score/src/dsl.rs:167–170`); `scale_for()` (`engine/src/automation.rs:11`) is an
explicit list of log-scaled targets, so new Hz targets must be added there.

**Existing analysis assets.** `explore/notch.py` and the skill's `notch-finder.py` already use a
CQT (1 bin/semitone, C2–B6, hop 512, `librosa.effects.harmonic`) for a per-note wrong-note list;
`explore/ops.py` has typed ops `cast.swap`, `track.eq_notch`, `track.hp`, `track.transpose`,
`clip.root`, `track.octave`, `track.release`, `track.volume`, `track.add_part`. Sample manifests
(`*.apricity.json`, `apricity_manifest: 2`) carry `notes[] {start, end, midi, velocity}`
(basic-pitch), `tonal.tuning_cents`, `tonal.beat_chroma`; fitfeat sidecars carry
`beat_tonalness`, `beat_bands_db (24)`, onsets, `beat_bass_share`. `optimize/objective.py`
combines penalty terms and one positive `contribution` term as `J = 100(1 − P) + 100·w_c·C`; the
whole-mix gate uses `check.py`'s objective with `WHOLE_MIX_MARGIN = −2.0`, fit to one verdict.

## 2. The octave-aware analyzer (design question 1)

### 2.1 Representation

`librosa.cqt(y, sr=22050, hop_length=512, fmin=C1, n_bins=252, bins_per_octave=36, tuning=τ·3)`
per pitched, non-kit stem, magnitude. Reasons, in order:

- **3 bins per semitone** gives ±33 ¢ neighbours for a parabolic sub-bin pitch fit (the cents
  correction) and lets a 30 ¢-sharp note still land in its semitone after the `tuning` shift.
  1 bin/semitone (the notch finder) can't give cents; 12 bins/semitone quadruples cost for nothing.
- **CQT not VQT**: VQT's higher-resolution bass bins have windows over a second long at 3/semitone
  and smear across beats; the bass is the register we trust the score for anyway (2.3).
- **`tuning` is in fractions of a bin** in librosa (the prototype passed cents/100 and was 3× off;
  fixed as `cents/100·3`), and `fmin = C1` exactly so bin `3k` is the centre of semitone `k`.
- Harmonic-template **NNLS**: activations `a ≥ 0` minimising ‖C_frame − T·a‖² where `T` is
  84 note templates, each with partial weights `[1, .6, .4, .3, .2, .15]` at `+0, +12, +19, +24,
  +28, +31` semitones (`scipy.optimize.nnls` per frame on the 252-bin vector; ≈ 0.4 ms/frame,
  ≈ 0.3 s for an 8-bar window). Output `A (84, n_frames)`.
- Weight frames by RMS × tonalness as today; **NNLS residual** ‖C − T·a‖/‖C‖ > 0.6 marks the
  frame *noisy* (a crash, a vocal breath) and it contributes to clash weighting but not to chord
  recognition. This is the inharmonic/noisy-source answer: a template fit that doesn't explain the
  frame is not a note.
- Per beat: the **median** activation over the beat's frames (robust to attacks), then a
  per-semitone local-max pick (a note's ±1-semitone leakage is not a second note). Keep `A_beat
  (n_beats, 84)` per stem next to the existing `chroma (n_beats, 12)` (which stays for the v1
  terms, so v1 numbers are reproducible).

### 2.2 Tuning offsets

Per stem: for every frame, the strongest CQT peak's parabolic offset `d = ½(a−c)/(a−2b+c)` on
log magnitude, folded to the semitone centre, giving cents in −50..50; the median is the stem's
offset τ. Validated on a synthetic +30 ¢ tone with six partials: **+29.8 ¢**. Per note (for the
steering report): the same fit at that note's bin, energy-weighted over the span. The correction
the report emits is `−τ` for the stem and, if the per-note spread exceeds 20 ¢, a note that the
stem's own tuning can't fix (a bent or inharmonic note) is flagged instead of "corrected".

The Emerge-swap `low` stem (Ave's "clean low A♭", pinned `Ab1`, moved to each root) reads
**+29 ¢ sharp** in the final prototype run. That is plausible (a pinned root is a semitone label,
not a cents label) and would be a real steering result (`clip low: retune −29 ¢`), but it is
**unverified**: the same stem read −10 ¢ before the tuning-units fix and `check.py`'s tuning guard
did not fire. Phase 1's first synthetic test (section 5.3) settles it.

### 2.3 What is analysed and what is known

- A track whose `stems.json` entry has `pitch` (a pitched single-note track: `voicing`, `notes`)
  is **not** analysed for notes. Its sounding pitches per beat come from the compiled timeline:
  Phase 1 adds `events` for pitched tracks to `stems.json` (`{track, start_beat, end_beat, midi}`;
  the compiler has them, `Timeline.events`) — a small Rust change in `stems_manifest`. Until it
  lands, the Python side derives the note from `chord`/`bass` + the track's `voicing`/`octave`
  (what the prototype did: the bass pc = the written bass).
- Loops (`transpose auto|follow|N`) and `warp repitch` one-shots are analysed as in 2.1.
- Kits and `pitched: false` tracks are excluded, as today.

### 2.4 Chord recognition of the combined result

Per beat (and per span, from the span's summed beat activations), sum the stems' `A_beat`
(each normalised to its own loudness, so a loud pad doesn't decide alone), then:

- **Bass** = the score's bass note when a pitched single-note track sounds this beat; else the
  lowest extracted note with ≥ 25 % of the loudest activation, at or above G1 (49 Hz).
- **Candidates**: 12 roots × {maj, min, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, 7, maj7, m7, mMaj7, ø7, °7} ×
  extensions {none, 6, 9, maj9, m9, add9}. Score = Σ activation mass on chord tones − 1.5 × mass
  off-chord − 0.05 per tone beyond three (parsimony) + 0.15 if the bass is a chord tone.
  Extensions only count when the extension note sounds **above C4** or ≥ a major ninth above the
  bass; otherwise it's scored as an off-chord tone (a 9th at 65 Hz is mud, not colour).
- Output per span: `heard {root, quality, extensions[], bass, inversion (root|1st|2nd|3rd),
  confidence}` where confidence = (best − second best) / best, plus per-note attribution.

### 2.5 The chord-quality term `Q` (positive, 0..1 per span)

`Q = 0.5·target + 0.2·extension + 0.15·spacing + 0.15·voice_leading`

- **target** = 0.5·[root matches] + 0.3·[bass matches the written slash bass, or the root when
  none] + 0.2·[the heard chord's tones ⊆ the written tones]. A `IV/3` is satisfied only when the
  heard bass is the third.
- **extension** = 1 when a written 7th chord is heard *with* its 7th; 0.5 when a triad is written
  and a 7th/9th is heard that is diatonic to the key (interesting) and above the register floor;
  0 otherwise. Non-diatonic extensions score 0 here and pay the clash term as today.
- **spacing** = 1 − (pairs of sounding notes ≤ 4 semitones apart below C3, per note below C3).
  This is where a written maj7 whose 7th sits a semitone under the bass *in the bass octave*
  loses points (E2 under F2 in the Fmaj7 spans — every candidate scored 0 here), while E3/E4
  over F2 does not. It replaces the pair kernel's blanket m2/M7 doubling for chord-tone pairs
  (2.6).
- **voice_leading** = max(0, 1 − mean nearest-note movement (semitones) between this span's and
  the previous span's note sets / 6). Rewards loops whose notes stay put across chord changes.

`Q` is only computed for a span whose beats have tonal mass ≥ 10 % of the render's median beat
mass (silence earns nothing) and whose bass (2.4) exists; else `Q = 0` for the span.

### 2.6 Combining with the clash penalty and the guards

`objective_v2 = consonance_v1' − Σ guards + 10 · mean(Q)` where `consonance_v1'` is v1's
consonance with one change to the pair kernel: a pair of pitch classes that are **both chord
tones of the current span** scores 0 in `INTERVAL_K` (the written maj7 stops being the worst
case); their register problem, if any, is `spacing`'s job. Everything else in `beat_clash`, the
bass-root term and the guards stays. Anti-gaming:

- `Q` reads the same activations the energy, mute and density guards read; muting the loop
  removes its clash *and* its `target`/`extension` (the bass alone hears as a bare root: target
  0.8, extension 0 → Q ≈ 0.55, below any real chord).
- The coverage guard (every chord tone ≥ 5 % of the span's tonal energy) keeps "play only the
  root" from scoring; a new **extension guard** flags a span where the heard extension carries
  > 40 % of the span's mass (a 9th louder than the chord is not colour).
- Weight 10 bounds `Q`'s reach to 10 points; the backtest (5.2) shows 20 over-reaches.

### 2.7 Rust implementation: crate layout, DSP pieces and their cost

**Crate `crates/apricity-harmony`** (new; depends on `apricity-theory` for `Chord`/`PitchClass`,
`serde`/`serde_json`, `rustfft`; optional `rayon` off on wasm, as `design/storage.md` does for
`apricity-data`). Modules and the code each needs:

| Module | What | Rust source | Cost (this Mac, 8-bar 6-stem window; **estimates**, unverified until task 2 lands) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cqt` | Sparse-kernel CQT (Brown & Puckette 1992): one FFT per frame, kernels precomputed once per (sr, fmin, bins); `n_fft` = next power of two above the longest kernel (C1 at Q≈51 → 1.56 s → 32768 at 22.05 kHz, or 65536 at 44.1 kHz). Input is resampled to 22.05 kHz with `apricity-dsp::resample` first. | `rustfft` 6.x (pure Rust, no `std::simd`, builds for `wasm32` and `aarch64-apple-ios`; ~1 MB compiled) + ~200 lines | ~690 frames × 32768-point real FFT ≈ 0.15 s; kernel MACs (≈ 3 % sparse of 252 × 16384) ≈ 0.1 s |
| `nnls` | Lawson–Hanson active-set NNLS, f64, fixed iteration cap (3 × 84) so every target iterates identically; the 252 × 84 template matrix `T` built once per tuning offset | ~120 lines, hand-written (no `nalgebra`); a tiny dense QR/least-squares helper (~60 lines) | 84 unknowns, 252 rows, typically < 30 active-set steps: ≈ 0.5 ms/frame → 0.35 s per stem, ~1.5 s for the window; per-beat medians and the rest are negligible |
| `pitch` | Parabolic sub-bin peak fit, per-stem and per-note cents (2.2) | ~20 lines | — |
| `notes` | Beat aggregation on the score grid, local-max note pick, tonalness/RMS weights (port of `check.py`'s `frame_tonalness`/`frame_rms` via an STFT that reuses `rustfft`) | ~150 lines | — |
| `chord` | Candidates × scoring (2.4), inversion, extensions, confidence | ~150 lines | 12 × 12 × 6 templates per span: microseconds |
| `quality` | `Q` (2.5), the chord-tone pair-kernel change, `objective_v2`, guards (2.6) — a port of `check.py`'s `evaluate`/`apply_guards` so the CLI can produce v1 *and* v2 without Python | ~500 lines (the port is the biggest single piece) | — |
| `steer` | Transposition maps, wrong notes, regions, suggestions; `serde` types for `steer.json` (schema 3.1) | ~300 lines | 12 rolls × spans × stems: microseconds |
| `io` | Reads `stems.json` + WAVs (`hound`, already a CLI dep — behind a `std` feature; wasm/UniFFI callers pass decoded `f32` buffers), sample manifests (`notes`, `tuning_cents`) and fitfeat sidecars (`.npz` = zip of `.npy`; ~80 lines to read the two arrays needed, or Phase 1 writes a `.fitfeat.json` twin from Python) | ~200 lines | — |

Total ≈ 1.8 k lines of Rust, one new dependency (`rustfft`; `hound` is already in the tree).
`basic-pitch`, beat tracking and CLAP stay in `analysis/` (Python, offline); the analyzer reads
their stored results and never calls Python. `essentia` is not needed: HPCP is replaced by the
CQT path for v2, and the v1 port computes chroma from the same CQT folded to 12 bins (a documented
deviation from Essentia's HPCP; the parity test for v1 numbers is therefore against the *ported*
Python, not against `check.py`'s HPCP — see task 3).

**Bindings.** `apricity-harmony` exposes one pure function,
`analyze(window: &Window, opts: &Options) -> Report` where `Window { tempo, meter, key,
offset_beats, spans, tracks: Vec<TrackAudio { name, pitched, kit, pitch, events, samples: Vec<f32>, sr }> }`,
and `Report` is `serde`-serialisable (`steer.json` is `serde_json::to_string(&report)`). Then:

- **CLI** (`apricity-cli`): `apricity check <stems dir> [--json] [--baseline] [--allow-mute]`
  replaces `scripts/check-stems.py`'s job (the Python script becomes a thin wrapper that shells
  out, so `renders/log.jsonl` keeps its shape); `apricity steer <stems dir> [--against written|heard] -o steer.json`.
- **wasm** (`apricity-web`): `analyze_json(window_json, samples: Float32Array[]) -> String`,
  so the web UI can score a `--stems` render it has in memory.
- **UniFFI** (the planned `crates/apricity-ffi`): `fn analyze(window: Window, opts: Options) -> Report`
  as `uniffi::Record`s.
- **Python**: no PyO3 crate exists yet (`design/storage.md` plans `apricity-ffi` for Swift and
  Python together). Phase 1 uses the **JSON CLI** (`apricity steer ... -o steer.json`, read by
  the optimizer with `json.load`); when `apricity-ffi` grows a PyO3 target, the same `analyze`
  is exported. The optimizer's surrogate (`optimize/surrogate.py`) keeps its Python terms; only
  the render-stage scoring moves to the CLI.

**Python reference + parity.** `analysis/apricity_analyze/harmony2_ref.py` is the
reference: `librosa.cqt` is *not* used (its kernel normalisation and windowing differ from a
straight Brown–Puckette kernel); instead the reference builds the same sparse kernel in numpy
so the two implementations compute the same thing, and `scipy.optimize.nnls` is the NNLS
reference. Fixed inputs are checked in under `analysis/tests/fixtures/harmony2/`: three synthetic
WAVs (the C/E chord, the +30 ¢ note, the Cm7 loop + A2 bass, each 2 s, 22.05 kHz, ≈ 90 kB) and
one real 4-beat excerpt of two stems from the Emerge window (≈ 700 kB) with its `stems.json`.
Tolerances: CQT magnitudes within 1e-5 relative (f64 FFT vs numpy's), NNLS activations within
1e-6 absolute after normalisation, cents within 0.5 ¢, chord recognition identical, `Q` within
1e-3, `objective_v2` within 0.01. The test runs on both sides (`cargo test -p apricity-harmony`
reads the fixtures and the reference's stored outputs `expected.json`; `pytest` regenerates
`expected.json` and diffs it against the checked-in copy so a drift in either side fails).

## 3. The steering report (design question 2)

Written by `apricity steer <stems dir> -o steer.json` (Rust, Phase 1), one file per render
window; the audition tool scores the **together** window (bars 9–16 of a 16-bar audition) by
rendering it with `--bars` so `offset_beats` aligns it, exactly as today. The optimizer and
agents read the JSON; the web UI gets the same `Report` through wasm.

### 3.1 JSON schema (draft; every field listed is produced in Phase 1 unless marked P2)


### 3.2 The 12-transposition map, and how it relates to the solver

For each loop stem and span, rotate the stem's span activation vector by `k ∈ −6..5` semitones
(a roll along the 84-note axis, i.e. real octave-aware pitch, not a chroma rotation), re-sum with
the *other* stems held fixed, and record `Q_k` and `clash_k`. The map is analytic: no render. The
example above is the prototype's whole-window map for the Emerge loop (0 best at 0.78, +4 next
at 0.51); the per-span map is what Phase 1 emits.

Relation to the solver: `apricity explain` shows the solver's choice and `runners_up` per chord
for the same loop, scored on the loop alone (`bright −5 st ... next best −2, +0, +2` under
`VII (G)`). The map scores the same candidates **with the other parts sounding**. When the map's
best differs from the solver's choice by more than a margin (proposed: ΔQ ≥ 0.2 or Δclash ≤
−0.05), the report emits a `track.transpose_span` suggestion. The solver itself is untouched in
Phase 1; Phase 3 can feed the map back as a `pairwise` weight in `solve()` (open question 3).

### 3.3 Wrong notes, cents, regions

- **wrong_notes**: per span, per stem, extracted notes whose pitch class is off the written chord
  (or off the heard chord when `--against heard`), with octave, Hz (equal temperament at the
  score's reference, plus the note's measured cents), share of the stem's span mass, and beats.
  Sorted by share × the v1 chord penalty for that pitch class (root/bass semitone first).
- **cents** per stem (2.2) and the correction op when |τ| > 8 ¢ (the guard's threshold).
- **regions**: spans with `Q ≥ 0.6` and `clash ≤ 0.10` are `fit`; contiguous runs are merged to
  bar ranges. The audition tool uses `regions.fit` to say "the together window works from bar 9
  to 14".

## 4. The chord-following EQ (design question 3)

### 4.1 DSP options

| Option | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **Bank of peaking biquads** (cut and/or boost at every non-chord/chord note in range) | Fits `process_chain`'s 32-frame re-parameterisation path; bit-exact; no latency; `Biquad::response_db` gives the designer a curve to print; ~56 biquads/channel (8 non-chord pcs × 7 octaves) = ~5 M ops/s at 48 k, trivial offline | A biquad notch is symmetric in log-f only approximately; very narrow notches (tolerance < 15 ¢, Q > 60) ring, so glide must interpolate coefficients, not jump |
| Comb / resonator bank (feedback delay tuned to the chord tones) | The classic "chordal resonator" sound | Only one fundamental per comb, partials are inharmonic-free but so are the *cuts* (a comb can't cut); harder to make "invisible"; a chord change is a delay-length jump |
| STFT spectral masking | Arbitrary mask shapes; can protect partials exactly | Phase/pre-echo artifacts with a wide window, poor bass resolution with a narrow one; ~2048-frame latency the loop-cycle model would have to compensate; expensive in the WASM build; not bit-exact across FFT libraries |

**Recommendation: the biquad bank**, with the comb sound recovered as the `boost` mode at high
depth and low tolerance (a peaking boost of +12 dB, Q 40 on every chord tone *is* a tuned
resonator bank).

### 4.2 The harmonic-series problem and `harmonics N`

A chord tone's partials land on non-chord pitch classes: for A minor (A C E), A2's 5th partial
is C♯5 and 7th is ~G5; E3's 5th partial is G♯5. Cutting those partials thins the chord tone itself
(the "hollow" sound of naive chord EQ). Rule: for every chord tone `t` (with octave, from the
span's `voiced` tones and the sounding bass) and `h ≤ N`, the frequency `h·f_t` is **protected**:
any cut band within `tolerance` of it is skipped. Default `N = 6` (partials up to the 7th, 31
semitones), which protects the audible colour of a bass note without turning the 5th-partial
major third into a hole in a minor chord (the C♯5 of A2 stays; at −9 dB of cut it would have
been the most audible artifact). `harmonics 0` is the "autotune-ish" setting the user described.

### 4.3 Architecture

- **Spec** (`apricity-score`): `Effect::Harmonic(HarmonicSpec)`; fields in 4.4 plus
  `spans: Vec<HarmonicSpan { start_beat, end_beat, tones: Vec<u8 /*midi*/>, bass: u8 }>` filled
  by the **compiler** from the resolved harmony (`ChordSpan.fit.chord_tones`, the chord's `bass`,
  `voiced(Voicing::Seventh)` from the bass upward for the octave placement). The engine never
  parses theory; a score without the effect compiles to the identical timeline (`spans` is on the
  spec, not the timeline).
- **Engine** (`apricity-engine/master.rs`): a new `Stage::Harmonic` inside `MasterChain`, or a
  dedicated arm in `process_chain` like `Effect::Comp` with sidechain. Per 32-frame block: beat =
  `(frame_in_loop / frames_per_beat) + offset_beats` → the current span; build the target band
  list (4.5); interpolate coefficients from the previous block's toward the target over `glide`
  (per-band linear ramp of `hz`/`db`, recomputing coefficients per block — 32 frames at 48 k is
  0.67 ms, well under any glide). Automation lanes (4.6) are read per block like every other
  effect. `mix` blends dry/wet per sample as `Comp.mix` does.
- **Bit-identical when absent**: the new arm is only reached for `Effect::Harmonic`; `params()`,
  `Stage` and the no-automation path are untouched. Acceptance test: render `examples/*.apr`
  before/after and diff the WAVs (the existing `no_automation_output_equals_previous_behavior`
  pattern), plus a unit test that a `harmonic` with `depth 0dB` is a no-op to within float
  rounding of the biquad (state passes through `1.0` coefficients — assert exact equality by
  bypassing the bank when depth is 0).
- **DSP** (`apricity-dsp/fx.rs`): `HarmonicBank { bands: Vec<Biquad>, targets: Vec<Band> }`,
  `Band { hz, db, q, active }`, reusing `BiquadKind::Peak`. The bank is sized once for the
  `range` (all notes of the 12 pitch classes in range: ≤ 96 bands) and bands are switched
  on/off (db → 0) rather than allocated per chord, so the glide is a gain ramp for bands that
  leave or join the chord, which is click-free. `apricity-dsp` keeps its zero dependencies
  (it builds for iOS today); the bank is plain `f64` biquads like `Eq`.
- **Python reference + parity** (`analysis/apricity_analyze/harmonic_ref.py`): the same band
  design (note list, protected partials, `Q` from tolerance) and the same RBJ peaking biquad
  (`scipy.signal` is *not* used for the filter itself, since coefficient formulas differ in
  rounding; the reference implements the RBJ cookbook formula in numpy exactly as `Biquad::set`
  does), applied per 32-frame block with the same per-band gain ramp. Fixed inputs under
  `analysis/tests/fixtures/harmonic/`: a 4-chord synthetic score (`Am7 Fmaj7 Dm7 G`, 2 beats
  each at 120 bpm) rendered by the engine *without* the effect to a 4 s, 48 kHz stem (≈ 770 kB),
  plus its span list. The parity test runs the Rust effect (via a `apricity-dsp` unit test that
  loads the WAV and the JSON span list) and the reference on that stem at three settings
  (cleanup, autotune-ish, both/8 ¢) and asserts the outputs match within **−80 dBFS peak
  absolute difference** (1e-4) and 1e-6 RMS; the band-design intermediate (the list of `(hz, db,
  q)` per span) must match exactly. Any rounding drift that exceeds it is a bug in one side, not
  a tolerance to widen.

### 4.4 Parameters

| Parameter | Range | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| mode | `cut` / `boost` / `both` | `cut` | cut non-chord notes; boost chord notes; both |
| depth | 0–24 dB | 9 dB | cut depth (negative gain) for `cut`; boost for `boost`; `both` takes `depth` for the cut and `boost` for the boost |
| boost | 0–18 dB | 6 dB | only for `both` |
| tolerance | 5–100 ¢ | 30 ¢ | half-width of every band; `Q = f / (f·(2^(tol/1200) − 2^(−tol/1200)))` ≈ 29 at 30 ¢, 8.7 at 100 ¢, 173 at 5 ¢ (the user's "notch tolerance") |
| harmonics | 0–8 | 6 | chord-tone partials protected from cutting |
| range | 20–20000 Hz, `lo..hi` | `80..4k` | notes outside are untouched |
| glide | 0–500 ms | 40 ms | ramp at chord changes |
| mix | 0–100 % | 100 % | wet share |
| tune | 400–480 Hz | 440 (or the score's reference if one exists — **unverified** whether the language has a score-level tuning statement; `docs/language.md` shows none) | reference for the band centres |
| voicing | `written` / `heard` | `written` | P2: follow the steering report's heard chord instead of the written one |

### 4.5 Reading the chord progression

Per block, the span is the one whose `[start_beat, end_beat)` contains the block's beat
(`offset_beats` applied, as automation does). Bands: for `cut`, every note in `range` whose pitch
class is not in `tones`, minus protected partials (4.2); for `boost`, every note in `range` whose
pitch class is in `tones`, with the bass's octave and above weighted full and the octave below
the bass at half depth (a boosted sub-octave of the bass is mud). Between spans, `glide` ramps
each band's gain; bands common to both chords don't move. A score with no `chords` line (no
harmony) makes `harmonic` a no-op with a compile warning.

### 4.6 DSL and automation

```apr
track bright  bars 9-40  volume 4  group music
  harmonic cut 9dB tolerance 30c harmonics 6 range 80..4k glide 40ms mix 100%
  automate harmonic.tolerance  25=30c  33=8c          # tightens into the drop
  automate harmonic.depth      step  1=9dB  25=0dB  33=12dB
```

Grammar additions, in `docs/language.md`'s style:

```ebnf
effect      = ... | "harmonic" [ "cut" | "boost" | "both" ] { DB | "boost" DB | "tolerance" CENTS
                   | "harmonics" INTEGER | "range" HZ ".." HZ | "glide" TIME | "mix" SHARE | "tune" HZ } ;
CENTS       = NUMBER "c" ;
TARGET      = ... | "harmonic.depth" | "harmonic.boost" | "harmonic.tolerance" | "harmonic.mix" | "harmonic.glide" ;
```

Allowed under a track, group or return (add `"harmonic"` to `TRACK_LINES`, `GROUP_LINES`,
`EFFECTS` in `dsl.rs:167–170`; not the master, like `filter`). Automation targets are linear
(cents, dB, %, ms) so `scale_for` needs no change; `harmonic2.depth` addresses a second instance
like `eq2.*`. Units: `c` for cents is new in the Units table.

- **cleanup** (invisible): `harmonic cut 6dB tolerance 20c harmonics 6 range 100..3k glide 60ms`
- **autotune-ish** (the user's description): `harmonic cut 14dB tolerance 40c harmonics 0 range 60..6k glide 15ms`

## 7. Risks and open questions (design question 6)

Risks:

- **Calibration on eight windows.** `Q`'s weights and the objective weight 10 rest on two verdict
  sets. The backtest harness (task 5) must run on every new listening-room verdict before the
  weights are trusted; keep `objective` (v1) in every log line so a regression is visible.
- **Prototype instability.** Three bugs each moved `Q̄` by up to 0.3. The real module must ship
  with the synthetic tests first (task 2 before task 3), and the C/E test decides NNLS.
- **Bass-register analysis.** The CQT's bottom octave leaks and the pinned bass read +29 ¢ and
  ghost notes; until the bass-stem sanity test passes, no `clip.retune` suggestion should be
  applied automatically.
- **Effect artifacts.** Narrow notches (tolerance < 15 ¢) ring; the glide must be a gain ramp,
  not a coefficient jump. The `both` preset at 8 ¢ is a creative effect and should not be a
  default anywhere.
- **Disk and build.** The Rust tasks touch up to five crates (`apricity-harmony`, `-dsp`,
  `-score`, `-engine`, `-cli`); pair each with a Python task rather than another Rust task when
  possible, and never render full songs for validation — windows only.
- **Cross-target determinism.** `rustfft` picks different kernels per CPU (AVX/NEON/scalar) and
  wasm has no SIMD by default, so CQT magnitudes can differ at the 1e-7 level between the Mac,
  the phone and the browser; NNLS active-set choices can flip on a near-tie. Mitigations: f64
  everywhere in the analyzer, the fixed NNLS iteration cap, tolerances (2.7) chosen above that
  noise, and chord recognition compared *as chords*, not as floats. If a flip still shows up in
  the parity test, add a deterministic tie-break (lowest index) rather than widening tolerances.
- **The v1 port drifts from HPCP.** `apricity check`'s v1 numbers come from CQT-folded chroma,
  not Essentia's HPCP, so the historical `renders/log.jsonl` objectives are not directly
  comparable to the ported v1. The backtest harness (task 7) re-scores the logged windows with
  both so the comparison is like for like; keep `check.py` runnable for one release.

Open questions for the user (with a recommendation each):

1. **Should 9ths/6ths be writable now (Phase 3 task 10) or only rewarded when heard?** Recommend:
   reward-when-heard first (Phase 1); add them to the DSL once `Q` is trusted, since a written
   `Am9` the loops can't supply just lowers coverage.
2. **How should a cents retune be written?** `root Ab1` pins a note; there is no clip-level cents
   option. Recommend a clip option `tune -29c` (a clean addition to `clip-option`), applied before
   the score's A440 retune.
3. **Should the solver learn the pairwise term (task 9) or stay a per-voice fit with the map as
   advice?** Recommend advice-only through Phase 2; the map + `track.transpose_span` gives the
   same result with a visible reason, and the solver's exhaustive search (13⁵) would grow with a
   pairwise term.
4. **Default mode and depth for `harmonic` when the optimizer adds it?** Recommend the cleanup
   preset (`cut 6dB tolerance 20c harmonics 6`), never `both`; creative settings are the user's.
5. **Is a maj7 voiced a semitone under the bass (E2 under F2) a clash or a colour in this genre?**
   The pair kernel says clash (doubled), the written chord says colour, `spacing` says mud below
   C3. Recommend: chord-tone pairs stop paying the kernel (2.6) and the register rule decides;
   confirm by ear on the Fmaj7 spans with and without `filter hp 100` on the loop.
